releases.author: Bahey-shalash
releases.description:
First release of Colors, a lean fork of [Fast Text Color](https://github.com/Superschnizel/obsidian-fast-text-color) by Leon Holtmeier, rebuilt around a single idea: the note stores a hex, so what renders is what is written.

```
~={#fb464c} colored text $x_{n}^2$ =~
~={#027aff}you can even ~={#e0de71}color=~ text inside colored text =~
```

## What's in it

- Hex-in-the-note markup: `~={#rrggbb}text=~`, with short form (`#0f8`) and alpha (`#ff880080`)
- Same output in live preview, reading mode and PDF export, since coloring is pure inline styles by construction
- Rendered LaTeX inside a colored section is colored too
- Colors nest
- Name-to-hex palette: menus and the command suggester show names, notes always receive the hex. Typing `~={yellow}` by hand is rewritten to its hex as the token completes
- Interactive delimiter: a color swatch in front of the visible hex, with a hover menu to change or remove the color
- Right-click → **Color**, plus commands for palette pick, custom hex, repeat last color, and remove
- Tab at the end of a colored section jumps out of it
- Settings are a flat list of name → hex rows. No themes, no per-id formatting, no generated CSS

## Differences from Fast Text Color

The markup syntax and the lezer grammar carry over. Rendering was rebuilt hex-only; themes, per-id formatting, the configurable keybind system and the floating color menu were removed by design. There is no migration step: notes using the original `~={id}` markup render whenever a palette entry carries that name, and editing such a token rewrites it to its hex.

## Install

Not yet in the community directory. Use [BRAT](https://github.com/TfTHacker/obsidian42-brat) with this repo's URL, or copy `main.js`, `manifest.json` and `styles.css` below into `.obsidian/plugins/colors/`.
